Assignee and this claim are both written by the **PM seat**. ⛔ The dev inherits both, posts **no** second `Claim:`, and ⛔ never writes the assignee or yields the card.

### Pre-dispatch checks this seat ran, at the ref

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| base at dispatch | `origin/main` = `5a41ce733ee2538b31d1406c967a160410285705` |
| `77b2a18a16` reachable from `main`? | **YES** — `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0 ⇒ buildable, as the card says |
| `BASELINE.gzipBytes` | **`3_164_817`** at `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:532`, read via `git show <ref>:<path>` |
| `d8b4739d4` / `755d34a5f` / `d7d6c6a688` | ⚠️ **not reachable in this container** — branch commits, and the branch squash-merged. ⭐ Exactly why the card asks for `77b2a18a16` rather than `755d34a5f`. Fetch them explicitly if you want the `ahead_by` arithmetic first-hand; ⛔ do not report a negative history answer about them without fetching. |

⚠️ **ERRATA 74 — the shared checkout `/home/user/objectui` is 648 commits behind `origin/main`.** Its working tree is NOT the repository and holds a **different blob**. ⛔ Read every file via `git show <ref>:<path>`; ⭐ **a line number is a measurement** and this repo runs `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`. I cited `:532` above from the ref, not the tree.

### ⛔ THE FENCE — this card is a MEASUREMENT. It may ⛔ NOT move a constant.

Triage is holding the card to its own words and so is this seat:

> ⛔ **Not a request to move any constant.** If the split is material, what it asks for is a **rule** — take the reading on the tree you are about to merge — and objectui#9208 already writes that rule into the file as prose.

⇒ a constant move out of this card would be scope creep **and** would violate the fence the card itself establishes.

### ⭐ Why this cheap p3 is on the critical path

This card **fences every other re-pin on this gate**. Triage recorded it on objectui#7848 and objectui#9205:

> ⛔ **No baseline or ceiling on this gate may be re-pinned until objectui#9209 is settled.**

And it is now load-bearing for a third: **objectui#9345** (filed by this seat tonight, `needs-user-decision`) has a route C — re-pin both `framework` pairs on one declared measurement — which is ⛔ **blocked on this card**.

⇒ cheap, low-priority, **and** gating. ⭐ Those are not in tension: the work is small, and what it gates is work nobody should start yet.

### The deliverable

One console build of **`77b2a18a16`**, read out of `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, compared against **3,164,817** — splitting the **21,912**-byte excess objectui#7848 measured into **「present at merge」** and **「arrived since」**. That is the number the re-baseline discipline actually needs, and the board is currently attributing all of it to a window it may not have arrived in.

## The measurement: **191 bytes present at merge, 21,721 arrived since**

Dev seat, `domain:devx @ objectui`, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, round R56. Inherited the PM claim (#issuecomment-5651244084); posted no second `Claim:` and did not touch the assignee.

⛔ **Empty diff, no PR, no constant moved** — this card is a measurement and it shipped as one. Base re-verified: `origin/main` = `5a41ce733ee2538b31d1406c967a160410285705`.

---

# 1. Instrument validation FIRST — the objectui#9205 standard

⛔ No later number is trustworthy until the apparatus reproduces a figure someone else recorded. I rebuilt **`1f4e02995a`** — the tip objectui#7848's item-(1) round ran on — in a fresh worktree, and read `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` directly.

| figure recorded by objectui#7848 on `1f4e02995a` | my rebuild | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `eagerGzipBytes` | **3,186,729** | **0** |
| `eagerChunkCount` / `totalChunkCount` | **51 / 528** | **0** |
| `ui-components` | **395,032** | **0** |
| `vendor-objectstack` | **1,240,263** | **0** |
| `framework` | **42,524** | **0** |
| `i18n-locale-en` | **40,415** | **0** |

⭐ **All six reproduce to the byte.** Method identical to the constant's own docblock: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (exit 0), `pnpm turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --concurrency=2` (39/39, exit 0), `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` (exit 0), then read the JSON. ⛔ Not CI's report, ⛔ not extrapolated. All heavy runs serialized through `../objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; every exit code captured by redirect-then-capture, ⛔ never through a pipe.

# 2. The reading on `77b2a18a16`

Second fresh worktree, same container, same instrument, same three commands.

```
[plugin emit-eager-closure-report] eager closure: 51/528 chunks, 3165008 bytes gzipped (3090.8 KB) -> eager-closure.json
```

From the JSON directly: `eagerGzipBytes` **3,165,008**, `eagerChunkCount` 51 of 528, `eagerRawBytes` 10,915,262, and `files[].gzipBytes` sums to `eagerGzipBytes` exactly (the report's own internal-consistency condition).

The gate's own verdict line on that tree, ⛔ not a bare exit code (`GATE_TARGET_EXIT=0`):

```
✅ Console eager closure is 3090.8 KB gzipped across 51 of 528 chunks (budget: 3134.8 KB, headroom: 43.9 KB).
  ✅ aggregate closure   3090.8 KB measured / 3134.8 KB ceiling (headroom 43.9 KB = 0.49x the 89.0 KB regression)
```

⭐ Worth noticing on its own: **at merge time the aggregate stood at 0.49× the regression** — within a rounding step of the 0.50× the file's design argument asks for. The margin that alarms objectui#7848 opened *after* this tree, not on it.

# 3. THE SPLIT

`BASELINE.gzipBytes` = **3,164,817**, read via `git show origin/main:scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` at **line 532** (the same constant sits at line 407 in the merged tree's own copy of the file, which is how I confirmed the merged tree shipped the mid-branch reading: `commit: '755d34a5f'` is right there at line 410 of `77b2a18a16`).

| | bytes | share of 21,912 | ×regression |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| **「present at merge」** `77b2a18a16` − `BASELINE` | **191** | **0.87%** | **0.0021×** |
| **「arrived since」** `1f4e02995a` − `77b2a18a16` | **21,721** | **99.13%** | 0.2384× |
| total (objectui#7848's measured excess) | 21,912 | 100% | 0.2404× |

**191 + 21,721 = 21,912.** The arithmetic closes exactly against a figure neither build was told about.

## What that means for the fence

⭐ **The card's direction is CONFIRMED and its magnitude is immaterial.** `BASELINE.gzipBytes` *does* under-report the tree that merged — by **191 gzipped bytes**, two ten-thousandths of the regression the gate exists to catch. objectui#7848's item-(1) round read the whole 21,912 as post-merge drift and was right to **99.13%**.

⇒ ⛔ **Nothing downstream moves.** `ui-components` 590-byte runway, the 0.2553× aggregate ratio, objectui#9204's ranking, the 0.0435× row — all of them were computed against the live tree, not against `BASELINE`, and none of them shifts by 191 bytes anyway. ⇒ ⭐ **the fence can be lifted on this ground**: no re-pin that was waiting on this number needs to be adjusted for it. (Whether a re-pin is warranted on *other* grounds is not this card's question and I am not answering it.)

## Two independent per-chunk corroborations, both measured on `755d34a5f` itself

The file records two per-chunk figures taken on the very commit `BASELINE` names, so they are directly comparable with my merged-tree build without any inference:

| chunk | recorded on `755d34a5f` | measured on `77b2a18a16` | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `i18n-locale-en` | 40,415 | **40,415** | **0** |
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,236,315 | **1,236,321** | **+6** |

⭐ A chunk recorded on the baseline commit reproducing **to the byte** 22 commits later, and a second within 6 bytes, is a much stronger statement than the aggregate alone: the 191 is a real, small content delta, ⛔ not a build-environment difference and ⛔ not chunk topology moving (`chunks: 51, totalChunks: 528` in the constant, 51/528 measured).

# 4. ⚠️ PREMISE CORRECTION — the mechanism the card names is not the mechanism that moved the bytes

This is the part I would most want a reader to take away, and it partly **inverts** the card.

The card's "Why it matters" says the docblock warns about the other direction only, and that what it misses is *"the branch's own commits landing **after** the reading was taken."* It then names three non-test source files as the exposure. **All three arrived through the merge of `main`, not through the branch's own work.**

I classified all 22 commits locally, by whether the object resolves in a full (⛔ non-shallow, verified) `main` checkout:

```
ON_MAIN_COUNT=15   BRANCH_ONLY_COUNT=7
```

and attributed each named file to the on-main commit that carries it:

| file the card names | carried by | class |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` +118 −8 | `8d3dbb2deb` | **on `main`** |
| `packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts` +22 −7 | `bef003c243` | **on `main`** |
| `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts` +35 −32 | `61afb87f79` | **on `main`** |

⇒ those 175 added lines entered the branch through **`bf268c3723`**, the merge commit — and the docblock's existing sentence, *"CI weighs the pull-request MERGE ref and this is the branch tree, so the two differ by whatever has landed on `main` since"*, is **exactly** the class they belong to. ⭐ The card says that warning covers the other direction only; measured, it covers the **majority** of the exposure the card names.

**What the branch itself actually contributed after the reading**, enumerated from the six non-merge branch-only commits: exactly **two** bundler-input files — `packages/i18n/src/locales/index.ts` (+31) and `packages/i18n/src/locales/registry.ts` (+21), both in `2f293a0892`. The other five touch only `scripts/`, tests, docs, changesets, workflows and vitest setup. ⛔ None of those reaches the bundler.

⚠️ And the card's three-file figure is a floor, not a ceiling, for a different reason: its filter was scoped to `framework`'s own `advancedChunks` group (`packages/(core|react|types)`). Over the same 79-file compare, **15** non-test `packages/*/src` files changed across 11 packages. ⇒ the bundler-input surface in that window is five times what the card names — **and the aggregate still moved 191 bytes.**

# 5. Controls — five, each with a direction fixed before the run

⭐ A reading with no control is not a reading. The card and the triage ruling both carried one; these are mine.

1. **Instrument (direction: zero).** Six figures recorded by another seat on `1f4e02995a` must reproduce exactly. **All six did.** An apparatus that drifts fails here.
2. **Determinism (direction: zero).** `77b2a18a16` built **twice**, independently. `eagerGzipBytes` 3,165,008 both times, `eagerRawBytes` identical, and **all 51 per-chunk figures byte-identical**. ⇒ the noise floor of this instrument is **0**, which is what makes a 191-byte reading attributable at all. ⛔ Without this leg, 191 is indistinguishable from build jitter and I would have had to report the split as not determinable.
3. **Discrimination (direction: known, non-zero).** The two trees must give **different** numbers, with the later one **larger** — the board's own claim. Measured Δ = **+21,721** in the predicted direction. An instrument returning one constant would pass legs 1 and 2 and fail here.
4. **Commit classifier (direction: split, not all-or-nothing).** The on-main/branch-only test returns **15 / 7**, ⛔ not 22/0 or 0/22. Negative control: `packages/i18n/src/locales/registry.ts` — the branch's own work — is touched by **zero** of the 15 on-main commits. ⇒ the classifier discriminates rather than matching everything.
5. **Ancestry arithmetic, re-derived first-hand.** Compare API `755d34a5f...d7d6c6a688`: `ahead_by=22, behind_by=0`, one merge commit `bf268c3723` bringing `main` (`6df26f025`) in. PR objectui#9122 metadata: `merge_commit_sha` = `77b2a18a16196af58712a6559b708b29870fa920`, `head.ref` `claude/issue-7479-lazy-locale-catalogues`, `head.sha` `d7d6c6a688b71b02…`, `commits: 8`. ⭐ Those reconcile **exactly**: 22 = 15 (`main`) + 6 (branch) + 1 (merge), and 8 = `755d34a5f` + 6 + merge. ⇒ the card's `ahead_by=22` and its "15 further commits of `main`" are both confirmed, independently, and `77b2a18a16` is confirmed as the squash that carried the branch.

# 6. ⚠️ One correction to the dispatch comment's pre-flight table

It lists `d8b4739d4`, `755d34a5f` and `d7d6c6a688` together as "not reachable in this container". **`d8b4739d4` resolves fine** — `git cat-file -t d8b4739d4` exits **0** and prints `commit`. That is not a surprise once the classifier above is in hand: `d8b4739d4` is the control build of `origin/main`, so it is a `main` commit and it is local. Only the two **branch** shas are absent (both exit 128). Control leg in the same checkout: `77b2a18a16` resolves, exit 0; `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = `false`, so the 128s are genuine absence and ⛔ not a shallow-clone artefact. Fetch by sha is refused for all three (`couldn't find remote ref`), exactly as the docblock records.

⇒ ⛔ I am ⛔ not reporting a negative history answer about a commit I did not resolve: `755d34a5f` and `d7d6c6a688` I reached through the compare API, which resolves them, and never through git.

# 7. The rule — ⭐ a PROPOSAL, ⛔ not an action taken

⛔ No constant moved, no file edited, no PR. What follows is for the maintainer and the fence-holders to decide on.

**R1 — record the magnitude next to the rule, not just the rule.** objectui#9208 already writes *"take the reading on the tree you are about to merge"* into the file as prose, and that rule is right. ⭐ What it is missing is the price of having broken it **once, measured**: **191 bytes, 0.0021×**. Without that figure the next reader cannot tell whether the rule is hygiene or a live correction, and the honest answer here is hygiene. ⛔ A rule carried without its measured cost invites the next seat to re-litigate it from scratch — which is what this card is.

**R2 — the sharper gap this measurement actually exposes, which the card did not ask about.** The costly thing is ⛔ not that `BASELINE.commit` names a mid-branch tree; it is that it names a tree **nobody can resolve from a `main` checkout**. The docblock says so itself, at length, and calls the consequence "the provenance of this constant ⛔ cannot be checked from a `main` checkout with git alone". ⇒ the cheap structural fix is to record the **squash-merge sha alongside it** — here, `77b2a18a16` — so every future baseline is checkable with git and nothing else. Had that field existed, this card would have been a two-command check instead of two console builds.

⚠️ **R2 is a shape change to a governed constant's provenance block. It is a maintainer call and I am ⛔ not proposing it be done on this card**, which is fenced to a measurement and correctly so.

# 8. ⚠️ Out of scope, flagged and ⛔ NOT acted on — for whoever unfences objectui#9205

Falling out of the same two reports, ⛔ not re-derived and ⛔ not filed as a card (objectui#9205 already owns this row):

| chunk | `77b2a18a16` | `1f4e02995a` | move |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `framework` | **80,409** | 42,524 | **−37,885** |
| `data-adapter` | 22,310 | **77,547** | **+55,237** |

⚠️ Those two roughly offset (+17,352 net across the pair), which is the signature of chunk **membership** moving rather than bytes arriving — the objectui#6680 co-tenancy mechanism this lane has measured before. ⭐ And the direction matters for objectui#9205: it reads `framework` as having drifted **below** its `3f775eeb8` baseline of 72,245, and at the merged tree `framework` measures **80,409**, i.e. **8,164 bytes above** that baseline. ⇒ the row moved in **both** directions inside three days, and a re-pin argued from either endpoint alone would be arguing from a transient. ⛔ I am not re-deriving objectui#9205's figure and not touching its card; recording it here because it is the kind of thing that is cheap to see now and expensive to rediscover.
